items.summary: ProcessorOptions passes unused fields through FileSyncStrategy to FileSyncOrchestrator

evidence: FileSyncStrategy.execute() signature takes ProcessorOptions but uses zero fields — it forwards the entire object to fileSyncOrchestrator.sync()
FileSyncOrchestrator.sync() takes ProcessorOptions but only reads: workDir, configId, dryRun, noDelete, hasAppCredentials — 5 of 10 fields
Unused at orchestrator: branchName, retries, executor, prTemplate, token
IWorkStrategy.execute and IFileSyncOrchestrator.sync both declare ProcessorOptions in their interface, so any substituted implementation receives fields it cannot meaningfully use

RunContext already exists as a narrower subset (workDir, dryRun, retries, token, executor) showing awareness of this pattern; the sync-specific subset (workDir, configId, dryRun, noDelete, hasAppCredentials) lacks an equivalent named type
detail.suggestion: Add a FileSyncOptions = Pick<ProcessorOptions, 'workDir' | 'configId' | 'dryRun' | 'noDelete' | 'hasAppCredentials'> in types.ts, and update IWorkStrategy.execute and IFileSyncOrchestrator.sync to accept it. SyncWorkflow.execute() constructs this narrower object before calling workStrategy.execute().

items.summary: Cluster of restating comments in updateManifest that echo the adjacent code

evidence: Line 236: '// File has deleteOrphaned: true, add to managed set' above 'newManaged.add(fileName)' — the condition already contains deleteOrphaned === true
Line 246: '// File was managed before but is no longer in config - delete it' above 'filesToDelete.push(fileName)' — restates what push() does and what '!has()' means

Lines 239-240: '// If deleteOrphaned is false or undefined, don't add to managed set / (explicitly setting false removes from tracking)' — the else branch is implicit; the parenthetical adds slight insight but could be a single tighter comment
Lines 251, 256: '// Build updated manifest, preserving other configs' and '// Update this config's managed files' — section labels that echo variable names (updatedConfigs, sortedManaged)
detail.suggestion: Remove or compress the restating comments. The outer block comment '// Process current config files' and '// Find orphaned files: in old manifest for this config but not in current config' are section labels that provide navigational value and can stay. The per-line comments inside the loops (lines 236, 239-240, 246) and the header comments on trivial assignments (lines 251, 256) should be removed — the code is self-explanatory at that level.

items.summary: safeCleanup (async) lives in type-guards.ts alongside sync-only type guard utilities

evidence: type-guards.ts exports: isPlainObject (sync), toErrorMessage (sync), safeCleanup (async: accepts () => Promise<void>).
Module name 'type-guards' signals a narrow scope of sync predicate/coercion utilities; safeCleanup is an async lifecycle helper with no relation to type checking.
Callers importing safeCleanup must import from a module that implies type predicates, which misrepresents the dependency.
detail.suggestion: Move safeCleanup to a more appropriate home such as src/shared/cleanup-utils.ts or src/shared/lifecycle-utils.ts, and update all importers. This removes the async/purpose anomaly from the type-guards module.

items.summary: withRetry() @throws AbortError is inaccurate: pRetry unwraps AbortError before propagating, so callers never observe AbortError

evidence: Docstring at line 179: '@throws AbortError for permanent failures, or the last error after all retries exhausted'
Implementation at line 199: 'throw new AbortError(error)' wraps the original error inside AbortError to stop pRetry
pRetry's documented behavior: when it receives an AbortError, it extracts the wrapped originalError and throws THAT to the caller — not the AbortError itself
Callers of withRetry() catching AbortError to detect permanent failures will never match: they receive the original error (e.g. ValidationError, SyncError) directly
detail.suggestion: Update the @throws annotation to accurately describe what callers receive: '@throws {ValidationError | SyncError | Error} The original error for permanent failures (pRetry unwraps AbortError before propagating), or the last transient error after all retries exhausted'. Alternatively add an inline note: 'Note: pRetry unwraps AbortError — callers receive the originalError, not an AbortError instance.'

items.summary: Interface-only symbols mixed between value imports and import type across ~15 files

evidence: ICommandExecutor (an interface) is value-imported in 15 files but import-typed in 6 others: authenticated-git-ops.ts, branch-manager.ts, commit-push-manager.ts, repo-lifecycle-manager.ts, types.ts, gh-api-utils.ts all use 'import type { ICommandExecutor }'.

In sync-command.ts, GitHubRepoInfo is correctly 'import type' (line 16) while RepoInfo from the same module is a value import (line 35) — inconsistent within the same file for symbols from the same source.
ILogger is value-imported in repository-session.ts but 'import type' in auth-options-builder.ts, repository-processor.ts, file-sync-orchestrator.ts, and pr-merge-handler.ts.
RepoInfo imported as plain value in pr-creator.ts and repository-session.ts (interface, never instantiated).
detail.suggestion: Add 'type' modifier to these interface-only imports: use 'import type { ICommandExecutor }' in all 15 value-import files, split mixed imports where needed (e.g. 'import { assertGitHubRepo } from' + 'import type { RepoInfo } from' for the same module). This is a mechanical multi-file edit with no behavioral change.

items.summary: Settings submodule tests split across flat root and subdirectories with duplicate coverage

evidence: test/unit/labels-diff.test.ts (306 lines) and test/unit/settings/labels/diff.test.ts (266 lines) both test the same diffLabels function from src/settings/labels/diff.ts — confirmed duplicate coverage from an incomplete migration.
All other lifecycle tests live in test/unit/lifecycle/ but lifecycle-report.test.ts remains in the flat root — inconsistent placement for a sibling file.
Rulesets have 4 tests at the flat root (ruleset-diff, ruleset-formatter, ruleset-plan-formatter, ruleset-processor) and 2 in test/unit/settings/rulesets/ — split location with no documented reason.

New tests added in the subdirectory structure (github-ruleset-strategy.test.ts, repo-settings-strategy.test.ts) while old tests remain at root — the migration started but stalled, leaving two competing conventions simultaneously active.
detail.suggestion: Complete the migration: move all settings-related tests from the flat root into their respective test/unit/settings/{labels,repo-settings,rulesets}/ subdirectories, deduplicate the overlapping labels-diff coverage, and move lifecycle-report.test.ts into test/unit/lifecycle/. Report the inconsistency; do not add new abstraction layers.

items.summary: p-retry@7.1.1 requires node>=20 but project declares node>=18 support

evidence: package.json declares engines: { node: '>=18' }
p-retry@7.1.1 package.json declares engines: { node: '>=20' }
p-retry is a production dependency used via src/shared/retry-utils.ts
detail.suggestion: Either: (a) update the project's engines field to node>=20 to match p-retry's actual requirement, or (b) downgrade to p-retry@6.x which supports node>=12 if Node 18 support is genuinely required.

items.summary: PRWorkflowExecutor.execute() converts all errors — including permanent auth failures — into a uniform success=false result

evidence: Lines 61-79 of src/vcs/pr-strategy.ts: catch(error) returns {success: false, message: `Failed to create PR: ${message}`} for all error types
Permanent errors (auth failures, token expiry) are indistinguishable from transient ones at the caller — both appear as PRResult with success=false
BasePRStrategy.executeMergeCommand uses withRetry which already discriminates permanent vs transient; PRWorkflowExecutor does not apply the same discipline to PR creation
detail.suggestion: Either re-throw permanent errors (using isPermanentError from retry-utils) so callers can handle them as fatal, or log at warn/error level when a permanent error is swallowed so operators can detect auth failures in CI logs.

items.summary: resolveGitHubToken logs app-token resolution failure at debug level even when no fallback token exists, making the failure effectively silent

evidence: Lines 207-214 of src/shared/gh-api-utils.ts: catch block uses log?.debug(...) regardless of whether envToken is present
When both app token resolution fails and envToken is absent, the returned {token: undefined, skipped: false} looks like 'no token manager configured' rather than 'auth resolution failed'
sibling pattern in checkAutoMergeEnabled (previously fixed) logs at warn for transient failures — this is less severe but the same category
detail.suggestion: Upgrade the log call to log?.warn(...) when envToken is also absent, so operators see a warning when authentication resolution fails with no fallback. The debug log for the fallback case is fine as-is.

items.summary: Lifecycle action rendering logic is duplicated between output/lifecycle-report.ts and output/unified-summary.ts

evidence: output/lifecycle-report.ts: renderActionDiffLines() iterates LifecycleAction[], dispatches on action type ('created', 'forked', 'migrated'), and emits diff lines including settings sub-lines.
output/unified-summary.ts: renderLifecycleLines() does the same dispatch with near-identical logic for 'created', 'forked', 'migrated' and settings sub-lines.

The two functions diverge only in minor formatting (lifecycle-report.ts prefixes with '+', unified-summary.ts prefixes with '+' too but omits the repo name from the created case). The structural pattern is otherwise identical, indicating a missed shared extraction.
detail.suggestion: Consolidate the action-to-diff-line rendering into a single exported function in output/lifecycle-report.ts (or a dedicated helper), parameterized for the minor formatting difference. unified-summary.ts should call it rather than maintain a parallel copy. This follows the pattern already used for formatCountEntry and renderSyncLines which are already shared across output modules.

items.summary: shared/repo-detector.ts mixes URL parsing, platform detection, display-name formatting, and type guards into one 38-importer hub

evidence: src/shared/repo-detector.ts is the most-imported file in the codebase (38 importers) and contains: parseGitUrl (URL parsing + platform detection), getRepoDisplayName (display formatting), isGitHubRepo / isAzureDevOpsRepo / isGitLabRepo (type guards), RepoInfo subtypes, and context interfaces. These are distinct capabilities bundled under a single file name that implies only URL parsing.
The mechanical scan flags 'responsibility_cohesion: 5 disconnected function clusters (15 functions) — likely mixed responsibilities' for this file, confirming the concern.

Callers needing only type guards must import from the same file as callers needing URL parsing, preventing the interface-segregation benefit that the rest of the codebase achieves through dedicated files.
detail.suggestion: Extract type guard functions (isGitHubRepo, isAzureDevOpsRepo, isGitLabRepo) and display helpers (getRepoDisplayName) into a sibling shared/repo-info-utils.ts (or similar name), leaving repo-detector.ts focused purely on URL parsing and the RepoInfo type definitions. This reduces the hub's blast radius and makes each file's responsibility self-evident from its name.

items.summary: Three vcs-layer methods declared async but never await, false async signal to readers

evidence: git-ops.ts:39: private async exec(command: string, cwd?: string): Promise<string> { return this._executor.exec(command, cwd ?? this._workDir); } with no await, async is redundant.
authenticated-git-ops.ts:42: private async execWithRetry(command: string): Promise<string> { return withRetry(...); } with no await, async is redundant.
authenticated-git-ops.ts:168: async lsRemote(branchName: string, options?: {...}): Promise<string>, both code paths (skipRetry and default) return Promises directly without await.
detail.suggestion: Remove the async keyword from all three methods: private exec(), private execWithRetry(), and lsRemote(). Each already returns a Promise<string> from the delegated call, so the async wrapper adds no value and misleads readers into thinking these methods contain awaited operations.

items.summary: validateRawConfig and validateForSync duplicate identical conditional-group probe lambdas instead of sharing a helper

evidence: validateRawConfig (lines 903-921) computes hasCondGrpFiles, hasCondGrpSettings, hasCondGrpPR with inline lambdas
validateForSync (lines 984-1002) computes the same three booleans with identical inline expressions — hasCondGrpFiles filter (k !== 'inherit' && cg.files![k] !== false) is verbatim duplicated
hasGroupFiles is already extracted as a shared helper (line 874), demonstrating the pattern exists; the conditional-group equivalents were not extracted
detail.suggestion: Extract hasConditionalGroupFiles(config), hasConditionalGroupSettings(config), hasConditionalGroupPR(config) helpers (or a single hasConditionalGroupContent(config) returning a flags object) mirroring the existing hasGroupFiles helper, and delegate from both validateRawConfig and validateForSync.

items.summary: toCreateRepoSettings called twice with the same input in runLifecyclePhase because the result is not surfaced by the helper

evidence: sync-command.ts:508-510: runLifecycleCheck receives repoSettings: ctx.config.settings?.repo and computes createSettings internally (lifecycle-helpers.ts:67)

sync-command.ts:517: the same ctx.config.settings?.repo is passed to toCreateRepoSettings again immediately after runLifecycleCheck returns, because LifecycleCheckResult does not include the createSettings that was already computed inside
The second call exists only to populate the lifecycle report input (lines 518-529) — information available from the first call is not propagated across the boundary
detail.suggestion: Add createSettings to LifecycleCheckResult (the return type of runLifecycleCheck) so the computed value is surfaced at the boundary, eliminating the recomputation and the dual-call pattern in the caller.

items.summary: runSettingsProcessor widens BaseProcessorResult to SettingsResult via unchecked cast

evidence: sync-command.ts:283-285: factory().process(...).then((result) => result as SettingsResult) — TypeScript accepts this only because BaseProcessorResult is a supertype, but SettingsResult adds planOutput and warnings which may or may not be present

sync-command.ts:238,254,270: a second cast layer in buildSettingsDescriptors assigns r as ProcessorResults['rulesetResult'] / labelsResult / settingsResult — these are structurally narrower types computed from the same widened SettingsResult
cli/types.ts:63-66: SettingsResult.planOutput is typed as { lines?: string[] }, a subset of the richer plan types in the settings modules, creating a shadow type that is never validated
detail.suggestion: Return the concrete processor result type from runSettingsProcessor and let logSettingsResult accept a union or a minimal interface that captures only the fields it actually reads (planOutput?.lines, warnings, skipped, success, message). Alternatively, add a runtime check or type predicate before accessing planOutput.lines to remove the need for the cast.

items.summary: getBuiltinVar() abbreviates 'Variable' to 'Var', inconsistent with codebase norm of spelling out domain nouns

evidence: Rest of codebase spells domain nouns in full: repoInfo, authOptions, envToken, tokenManager, repoName — no other abbreviations of this form exist
getBuiltinVar is a package-internal function; renaming to getBuiltinVariable has zero external impact
detail.suggestion: Rename to 'getBuiltinVariable' to align with the codebase norm of spelling out domain nouns fully.

items.summary: CommitPushManager.handleCommitError() uses generic 'handle' verb that obscures its classify-and-rethrow logic

evidence: Method is named handleCommitError but its body inspects the error type, decides whether to suppress or rethrow, and logs accordingly — the name reveals none of this decision logic
Rename candidates: classifyCommitError, handleUnexpectedCommitError, or rethrowIfUnexpectedCommitError would communicate the behavior without requiring a reader to open the implementation
detail.suggestion: Rename to 'rethrowIfUnexpectedCommitError' or 'classifyAndRethrowCommitError' to make the decision logic visible from the call site.

items.summary: src/shared/branch-utils.ts has fan_in=1 and belongs closer to its sole consumer

evidence: branch-utils.ts exports sanitizeBranchName() and validateBranchName(), imported only by src/cli/sync-command.ts.
grep search confirms zero other importers across all production source files.
shared/ is semantically a cross-cutting utilities layer (avg fan_in=11.8); a file with fan_in=1 used only at the CLI layer does not match that profile.
The file has no inbound dependency pressure from vcs/ or sync/ modules that would justify keeping it in shared/.
detail.suggestion: Move src/shared/branch-utils.ts to src/cli/branch-utils.ts (or inline its two small functions into sync-command.ts if they are not expected to grow). Migration steps: (1) copy file to src/cli/branch-utils.ts, (2) update the import in src/cli/sync-command.ts from '../shared/branch-utils.js' to './branch-utils.js', (3) delete src/shared/branch-utils.ts, (4) run `npm run build && npm test` to verify. If branch validation is expected to be reused by sync/ in the future, leave it in shared/ and document the intent.

items.summary: Test temp directories created in process.cwd() instead of tmpdir(), leaving artifacts in source tree on crash

evidence: manifest.test.ts:17: const testDir = join(process.cwd(), 'tmp-manifest-test')
index.test.ts:13: const testDir = join(process.cwd(), 'test-cli-tmp')
sync-command.test.ts:35: const testDir = join(process.cwd(), 'test-sync-cmd-tmp')
graphql-commit-strategy.test.ts:37: const testDir = join(process.cwd(), 'test-graphql-commit-strategy-tmp')
15 total occurrences across 8 test files
.gitignore only excludes 'tmp/' — named dirs like 'test-cli-tmp', 'test-sync-cmd-tmp' etc. are not covered
Sibling tests in sync/ (branch-manager, file-writer, etc.) correctly use tmpdir() — inconsistent practice within the same codebase
detail.suggestion: Replace process.cwd() with tmpdir() from node:os (already imported in the sibling tests that use it correctly). E.g., change 'join(process.cwd(), "test-cli-tmp")' to 'join(tmpdir(), "test-cli-tmp-" + Date.now())'. Alternatively, add the named patterns to .gitignore as a safety net.
